entries.090066c6e79cf51f: It is a category that sells workflow products as package software. 'X-point' features intuitive input forms similar to writing on paper. New license sales ended as of March 2022, and it now only provides support services and sells additional licenses. 'AgileWorks' inherits the functions of 'X-point' and is a product optimized for the operation of large organizations, with enhanced support for organizational restructuring and personnel transfers, and multilingual support. Revenue for the fiscal year ended March 2026 was ¥1,235 million, down 12.1% year on year, with product revenue of ¥185 million for 'X-point' and ¥1,049 million for 'AgileWorks'.
entries.1c3b7c8a801d0852: With a cumulative total of more than 5,000 adopting companies, the company states that its application forms, built with Java technology, offer operability "like paper." The company does not customize products for individual adopting companies; requests are reflected in version upgrades as needed, which it says allows development resources to be concentrated on strengthening product capability. The company states that it secures competitive advantage through a UI thoroughly designed from the user's perspective, the ability to operate systems in-house, extensive integration with other companies' systems, and its maintenance service structure.

entries.7bd271b9e230f536: Its management philosophy is "Smoothing connections among people, work and organizations to co-create a future full of growth and smiles," and its ideal is "The power of workflow for all companies." Against the backdrop of expanding workflow and cloud service markets, the company states that it aims to increase sales of AgileWorks, aimed at large and mid-sized companies, and of the cloud services X-point Cloud and AgileWorks cloud version. Its stated challenges are strengthening product functionality and expanding new services, strengthening its sales structure and brand recognition, and promoting work style reform and DX, and it positions workflow systems as "First DX," the first DX that companies undertake.
